bull_bear.body:
- Structural domestic demand-supply mismatch in ABS — consumption in India is voluminously larger than the combined output of domestic manufacturers
- In-house DSIR-recognised R&D Center at Abu Road, supported by JV partner Nippon A&L Inc. for new-recipe/application development; developed 12 new grades, improved 15 grades and 169 new colour grades in FY 2025-26
- Long-term contracts for basic raw material supply and maintenance of appropriate inventory levels to manage import-dependency risk on Styrene and Acrylonitrile monomers
- Zero Debt Company, sustaining operations and growth through internal accruals
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Import dependency and FX exposure on key raw materials — Styrene and Acrylonitrile monomers (together more than 85% of raw material composition) are entirely import-dependent as there is no indigenous producer; only Butadiene monomer (~15% by weight) is domestically available, exposing the ABS business to foreign exchange fluctuation risk.
- Raw material price volatility risk — Domestic ABS manufacturers deliberately keep low inventories of imported key monomers to limit the risk of price fluctuations; a drastic fall in international monomer prices (driven by unpredictable swings in crude oil, benzene and ethylene prices) can result in huge inventory-related losses.
- Single business segment concentration — The Company deals with a single business segment — manufacturing of ABS and SAN resins — with no diversification into other product lines or businesses.
- Geopolitical/energy-supply shock from the Middle East conflict — War in the Middle East since 28 February 2026 and closure of the Strait of Hormuz threaten a large-scale global energy crisis; the duration and scale of the conflict will determine the size of the shock to feedstock costs (crude oil, benzene, ethylene-linked) and to global economic activity.
- Downside global growth scenarios — Under the IMF's adverse and severe scenarios, global growth could fall to 2.5% (adverse) or around 2% (severe) with inflation rising to 5.4%-6%, which would weigh on demand for the Company's products and on input-cost volatility.
- Rupee depreciation / India macro risk — India slipped to the 6th largest economy globally (per IMF April 2026 WEO) partly due to ~11% rupee depreciation against the dollar, which is directly relevant given the Company's high dependence on imported monomers priced in foreign currency.

business.body: Bhansali Engineering Polymers Limited manufactures Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) and Styrene Acrylonitrile (SAN) resins, categorised as Highly Specialized Engineering Thermoplastics, and deals in a single business segment. Manufacturing is carried out at plants in Abu Road (Rajasthan) and Satnoor (Madhya Pradesh), with resins supplied to OEMs and MSME accounts serving automobiles, home appliances, electronics, healthcare and other moulded-plastic applications, predominantly within India with a small export component.

outlook.body:
- Complete the ongoing ABS capacity expansion from 75,000 TPA to 1,00,000 TPA to address the structural domestic demand-supply mismatch in ABS
- Leverage the in-house, DSIR-recognised R&D Center (supported by JV partner Nippon A&L Inc.) to continuously develop new resin grades and colour grades, sustaining customer loyalty and margins
- Maintain long-term contracts for basic raw materials and appropriate inventory levels to manage import-dependency and FX risk on Styrene and Acrylonitrile monomers
- Pursue energy-saving measures through efficient equipment and alternative sources of energy
- Sustain business operations and growth through internal accruals, preserving Zero Debt status
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is executing an ABS capacity expansion from the existing 75,000 TPA to 1,00,000 TPA. Orders for critical long-delivery equipment have been placed, and the balance engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) work is in progress; commissioning of the enhanced capacity is expected to be completed by end of September 2026. Separately, the in-house R&D Center at Abu Road (DSIR-recognised) added new testing/measurement infrastructure during the year — a low-temperature chamber for impact testing (relevant to auto-market grade development), a temperature-and-humidity controlled chamber, and technology to measure VOC in the Company's products.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Immense scope for growth in ABS given the existing demand-supply mismatch: domestic ABS consumption is voluminously larger than the combined output of domestic manufacturers
- Automobile industry recorded its highest-ever annual sales (~2.83 crore vehicles, up 10.4% YoY) in FY2025-26, a key demand driver as ABS resins are used across two/three/four-wheelers
- Household appliances demand remains strong, with rising adoption of premium, energy-efficient and smart-home products driving demand for engineering plastics; ABS finds extensive use in appliance housings, interior components and control panels
- Auto component industry growth (9.6% YoY in FY25) driven by higher OEM supply, exports and aftermarket demand supports downstream ABS consumption
- India's macro growth outlook remains supportive: FY26 real GDP growth of 7.6% and FY27 consensus of 6.8%-7.0%, aided by government capex, Make in India/PLI schemes and manufacturing push
- Threat: deliberate low-inventory practice by domestic manufacturers for imported key raw materials (Styrene and Acrylonitrile, >85% of raw material basket) to limit price-fluctuation risk, exposing the business to swings in crude oil, benzene and ethylene prices
- Global macro overhang from the Middle East conflict (Strait of Hormuz disruption) creates downside risk to energy prices and global growth, which the company is navigating with existing plans
